name: Singri ki Sabzi
instructions: 1. Wash the dried sangri thoroughly and soak them in water overnight. 2. Drain the water and boil the sangri in fresh water until tender, then drain again. 3. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan and add cumin seeds and asafoetida. 4. Add the turmeric, coriander powder, and red chili powder, stirring quickly to avoid burning. 5. Add the boiled sangri and salt, sautéing for 5 minutes. 6. Reduce the heat and pour in the whisked curd, stirring continuously until the sauce thickens and coats the sangri. 7. Sprinkle garam masala, garnish with fresh coriander, and serve hot with bajra roti.
description: Singri ki Sabzi is a traditional dish from the arid regions of Haryana. It makes use of 'Sangri', a hardy desert bean, which has been a staple source of nutrition for centuries in the dry climate. It is considered a nutritious, protein-rich dish often prepared during festivals and special community gatherings.
